video_title: Deshaun Watson Keeps Winning... What Happens to Shedeur?

quotes.speaker: Matt Barnes
quotes.summary_phrase: Deshaun Watson finding his footing again with the Browns
quotes.excerpt: I'm happy to see Deshaun Watson kind of find his footing again
quotes.quote: I'm happy to see Deshaun Watson kind of find his footing again, because he went through a lot. A lot of off-the-field stuff, the crowd not fucking with him, him not fucking with the crowd, up and down performances, tore his Achilles, and obviously getting a huge contract. But I say all that to say he's out there, looks like he's having fun again, and I think people quickly forget how good he was in Houston.

quotes.speaker: Stephen Jackson
quotes.summary_phrase: Deshaun Watson's resilience in returning to form
quotes.excerpt: He showed a lot of resolve and he's had his ups and downs
quotes.quote: He was a beast, and it's tough to regain that greatness when you haven't played in two to three years. You know, to come back, and like you said, he went through a lot, and he showed a lot of resolve and he's had his ups and downs. I'm not the guy to judge you what's happening off the field, but at some point, you got to understand you got to do better. You got to clean it up. Nobody's fucking perfect, we all make mistakes, we've all had our situations, it's life.

quotes.speaker: Stephen Jackson
quotes.summary_phrase: Browns' roster and coaching system supporting Deshaun Watson
quotes.excerpt: They put a good system around him, they got a good team
quotes.quote: Monken came in as the head coach, they put a good system around him, they got a good team, they got a lot of young talent offensively, they got a really good defense. They just needed a quarterback to go in and pretty much man the ship, and they're number one in the division with the Ravens, with Pittsburgh and Cincinnati. They're one. Nobody in the off-season said the Browns after six weeks would be one in the division and four and two with Deshaun starting at quarterback.

quotes.speaker: Matt Barnes
quotes.summary_phrase: Will the Browns keep starting Deshaun Watson over Dorian Thompson-Robinson?
quotes.excerpt: If Deshaun Watson continues to play well, do you see Dorian Thompson-Robinson staying there another year

text_blocks.speaker: Matt Barnes
text_blocks.text: If Deshaun Watson continues to play well, do you see Dorian Thompson-Robinson staying there another year as the potential backup going into year three, or do you think he hits the market?

text_blocks.speaker: Stephen Jackson
text_blocks.text: One, Dorian Thompson-Robinson didn't put the pressure on the position by coming into the league, and I say that by saying he wasn't a top pick. If you're a number one pick, if you're a top ten pick, then you put the pressure on the position right away. What coaches do, they evaluate. We don't see practice, as players we did, so when the starters came out, we knew why certain players were starting. The average fan, they don't see practice, they don't see who has command, they don't see who runs the room.

quotes.speaker: Stephen Jackson
quotes.summary_phrase: Dorian Thompson-Robinson's development compared to Russell Wilson
quotes.excerpt: If he was ready and he was like a Russell Wilson who came in second or third round
quotes.quote: If he was ready and he was like a Russell Wilson who came in second or third round pick for Seattle, and they had just paid a lot of money for I think Matt Flynn who was behind Aaron Rodgers at Green Bay. They paid him a bunch of money to come be the starter, and then you bring in second, third rounder like Russell Wilson and we're like, oh no, wait, wait, we got a problem. This dude is way better than the dude we just paid, he's going to start. And it comes to fruition and you see it, that wasn't the situation. So I know there's a lot of hype and it's the hype behind the name or the lineage where you come from or what you're actually doing on the football field.

quotes.speaker: Matt Barnes
quotes.summary_phrase: Who is the most feared defensive player in the NFL?
quotes.excerpt: Who do you feel like the most feared defensive player in the game right now?
quotes.quote: Who do you feel like the most feared defensive player in the game right now?

quotes.speaker: Stephen Jackson
quotes.summary_phrase: Top defensive players in the NFL
quotes.excerpt: TJ Watt, a healthy Micah Parsons, Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett
quotes.quote: TJ Watt, a healthy Micah Parsons, Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett. That's why it's hard to give you one. I can throw Jalen Carter, there's a bunch more, but I gave you those because with those players, Matt, they're the most double-teamed, they're the most chipped, they're the most that teams offensive coordinators slide the protection to.

quotes.speaker: Stephen Jackson
quotes.summary_phrase: Why Myles Garrett is the most feared defender
quotes.excerpt: If I had to pick one, I would probably pick Myles Garrett
quotes.quote: Aaron Donald over 1,500 double teams while he was playing. Myles Garrett has more slide protection, more chip blocks, and more double teams in ten years probably than anybody. TJ Watt, the production, same, chipped, slide protection, all that. But if I had to pick one, I would probably pick Myles Garrett, just because I've seen offensive coordinators try every single way to block this man. Even when they double team him, he gets home. Even when they chip him, he gets home. And he broke the sack record. Like legitimately, he legitimately broke the sack record and owns the record.
